description:
FILED s473t1 (Opus, the 13-file early-stop triage).  PRE-EXISTING.

REPRO (scratch/s473t1/probe/local-stdout.pl):

    print "before\n";
    { local *STDOUT; no strict "subs"; print "SHOULD-NOT-APPEAR"; }
    print "after\n";

    perl 5.40.3:  before / after            (the glob is emptied: the print
                                             goes to an unopened handle)
    PCL        :  before / SHOULD-NOT-APPEARafter

COST: perl-tests/yadayada.t, its whole 1-row shortfall.  The file's last loop
evaluates each of four one-line programs inside
`eval qq { {local *STDOUT; no strict "subs"; $line;} pass $mess; 1 }`.  For
`print 'D' ... 'A';` PCL writes DEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ to real stdout, and
the harness's next line comes out as

    DEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZok 32 - Parsing '...' in "print 'D' ... 'A';" ...

which matches no TAP row regex, so the assertion PASSED and was still counted
as missing (planned 34, produced 33).  This is the TAP-interleave hard rule
(fable-answers-s331): output that is not line-atomic costs a verdict.

The range answer itself is right (perl also gives DEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ for
`'D' ... 'A'` in list context) -- only the handle is wrong.
subject: `local *STDOUT` does not detach the handle -- the block's output still reaches real STDOUT and GLUES itself to the next TAP line, costing the row its verdict
